newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Dolenjska bank considers merger this year.
newsitem.headline: Dolenjska bank considers merger this year.

text.p: Slovenian bank Dolenjska Banka said on Thursday it was considering a merger with another domestic bank and said the link-up could happen as early as this year.
"We are ready for merger talks with any interested banks in Slovenia. The merger could happen as early as this year," Milena Dular, deputy chief executive of Dolenjska Banka, told Reuters.
She declined to give any further details.
Dolenjska bank, with a market share of 3.1 percent, is one of 28 Slovenian banks operating in the nation's overcrowded financial sector.

Analysts say mergers are inevitable as banks try to cut costs and prepare for future foreign competition. Parliament is expected to pass a law this year enabling foreign banks to establish full branches in Slovenia.
In October last year Gorenjska Banka and UBK said they were in merger talks. In January Noricum bank merged with Celje.
